title: Semi-stable extensions
description: Semi-stable extensions: admissible sets whose range (the set and everything it attacks) is maximal; credulous acceptance is Sigma-2-complete (Dvorak and Woltran). The check only needs the candidate's range, so the interface atoms are the derived atoms range/1 rather than the guessed in/1, and a refinement removes every set whose range is too small. The sample framework has no stable extension, three preferred and two semi-stable ones.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The framework. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): admissible sets, and their range.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: an admissible set, that is, a set that is conflict-free and attacks
% all its attackers.
{ in(A) } :- arg(A).
:- in(A), in(B), att(A,B).
beaten(A) :- in(B), att(B,A).
:- in(A), att(B,A), not beaten(B).
% Its range: the members and the arguments they attack.
range(A) :- in(A).
range(A) :- beaten(A).
#show in/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the range of the set (derived atoms), not its members.
fragments.text:
% The check compares ranges only.
glue(range(A)) :- arg(A).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for an admissible set with a larger range (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an admissible set whose range contains the candidate's range and
% one more argument.
{ big(A) } :- arg(A).
:- big(A), big(B), att(A,B).
hit(A) :- big(B), att(B,A).
:- big(A), att(B,A), not hit(B).
wide(A) :- big(A).
wide(A) :- hit(A).
:- range(A), not wide(A).
gain(A) :- wide(A), not range(A).
wider :- gain(A).
:- not wider.
#show big/1.

% The counterexample refutes every set whose range stays inside its range and misses
% one argument of it. So: an argument outside the wider range enters the candidate's
% range, or the first gained argument does.
relevant(range(A)) :- arg(A), not wide(A).
relevant(range(A)) :- gain(A), not gain(B) : arg(B), B < A.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% An argumentation framework without a stable extension (z attacks itself).
arg(a;b;c;d;e;f;g;h;i;j;z).
att(a,b). att(b,a).                 % a and b attack each other
att(i,j). att(j,i).                 % so do i and j
att(b,j). att(j,b).                 % and b and j
att(b,c). att(c,d). att(d,e). att(e,c).     % b attacks the cycle c, d, e
att(j,f). att(f,g). att(g,h). att(h,f).     % j attacks the cycle f, g, h
att(z,z).

generators.name: af-gnp
generators.description: A random argumentation framework: n arguments, each attack X -> Y with probability p/1000.
generators.text:
% af-gnp: arguments 1..n; each ordered pair (also X = Y) attacks with probability p/1000
arg(1..n).
att(X,Y) :- arg(X), arg(Y), @flip(p, X, Y) = 1.

#show arg/1.  #show att/2.

readme:
# Project: argumentation: semi-stable extensions

## Research question

Semi-stable extensions maximise the range. Does an interface of derived atoms (`range/1`) give stronger refinements than one of guessed atoms (`in/1`), and by how much?

## Baseline

2 solutions (exhausted) after 7 candidates and 5 clauses (0.06 s) on the example.

## Things to try

- A variant whose interface is `in/1` and a campaign on generated frameworks (copy the `af-gnp` generator from `af-preferred`).
- Stage extensions: change the check and compare the loops.
- Count the candidates per instance size and fit the growth.

## How to measure

Add the variants, write a suite over the instances (Campaign tab, Advanced mode), and read the instance × variant matrix; headless: `node tools/bench.mjs <id> --suite NAME --out rows.jsonl` and `node tools/report.mjs rows.jsonl`. Check every variant against the `reference` loop (or the audit) on small instances before trusting its numbers.
